request.system: You are an experienced audio electronics technician diagnosing a unit on the bench. Exactly one component has failed. messages.content:
Circuit: Block 4 - Op-amp make-up gain stage. Single-supply non-inverting stage (gain 11) biased at half supply (7.67 V). Behavioural FET-input op-amp with 3 MHz gain-bandwidth and outputs limited to 1.5 V inside each rail.

Stages: opamp = Op-amp gain stage

Parts:
- C401: film_cap 1u (stage opamp)
- R401: resistor 100k (stage opamp)
- R402: resistor 22k (stage opamp)
- R403: resistor 22k (stage opamp)
- C402: electrolytic 47u (stage opamp)
- U401: opamp TL071-class (stage opamp)
- R404: resistor 100k (stage opamp)
- R405: resistor 10k (stage opamp)
- C403: electrolytic 22u (stage opamp)
- R406: resistor 100 (stage opamp)
- C404: electrolytic 10u (stage opamp)
- C405: film_cap 100n (stage opamp)
- R407: resistor 100k (stage opamp)

Netlist of the healthy circuit (SPICE; node names as in the test points):
* Differential reference circuit - Block 4: op-amp make-up gain stage (standalone)
* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
* Original generic design written for this project. Single-supply non-inverting
* amplifier (gain 1 + R404/R405 = 11) biased at half supply by R402/R403 with
* C402 decoupling; R401 references the input to the bias node; C403 sets unity
* DC gain; R406 isolates the output; C404 couples to the next stage; C405 is
* the supply decoupling capacitor; R407 holds the output at 0 V DC. U401 is the behavioural op-amp in
* circuits/lib/devices.lib (GBW 3 MHz, output within 1.5 V of each rail).
* Parameter nodes: pgbw_u401 (MHz), pdead_u401, prail_u401.
* Fixtures: 15.3 V bench supply, source with 20k output impedance (tone-control
* output), 20k load (line-driver input).
* Run standalone: ngspice -b circuits/opamp/opamp.cir
* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
.include ../lib/devices.lib

* ---- Fixtures ----
VREG_BENCH vreg 0 DC 15.33
VIN_O op_src 0 DC 0 AC 1 SIN(0 0.0636 1k)
RSRC_O op_src tone_out 20k
RLOAD_DRV drv_in 0 20k

* ---- Op-amp stage ----
C401 tone_out op_in 1u
R401 op_in vref 100k
R402 vreg vref 22k
R403 vref 0 22k
C402 vref c402_esr 47u
RESR_C402 c402_esr 0 3.95
XU401 op_in op_fb op_pin vreg 0 pgbw_u401 pdead_u401 prail_u401 OPAMP_BEH
VPGBW_U401 pgbw_u401 0 DC 3
VPDEAD_U401 pdead_u401 0 DC 0
VPRAIL_U401 prail_u401 0 DC 1
R404 op_pin op_fb 100k
R405 op_fb r405_c 10k
C403 r405_c c403_esr 22u
RESR_C403 c403_esr 0 8.44
R406 op_pin op_out 100
C404 op_out c404_esr 10u
RESR_C404 c404_esr drv_in 13.3
C405 vreg 0 100n
R407 drv_in 0 100k

.control
set noaskquit
op
print v(op_in) v(op_fb) v(op_pin) v(op_out) v(vref) v(drv_in)
ac lin 1 1000 1000
print mag(v(op_pin)) mag(v(drv_in))
ac lin 1 20000 20000
print mag(v(drv_in))
.endc
.end

Test points:
- TP12: node tone_out, Op-amp stage input (stage opamp)
- TP13: node op_in, Op-amp non-inverting input (stage opamp)
- TP14: node op_fb, Op-amp inverting input (stage opamp)

content.text: I'll start by measuring the DC voltages across the stage.

content.thinking: TP13 reads 0.775 V instead of 7.58 V while vref is fine, so R401 (open or drifted high) or a shorted C401 is the likely culprit. I'm measuring TP12 next to tell them apart.
With TP12 at 0 V and C401 shorted, TP13 should read about 1.27 V, but the measured 0.775 V fits a drifted R401 better, so I'm checking the AC gain at TP13 to tell the cases apart.
